#SETUP

Importing provided data and loading libraries.
```{r}
# 1. Load the data ------------------------------------------
library(e1071)
library(readxl)
UniversalBank <- read_excel("C:/Users/Mike/Downloads/UniversalBank.xlsx")
View(UniversalBank)
```

Create a variable for the credit card value and then separate the data into training and testing data.
```{r}

UniversalBank$CC <- UniversalBank$CreditCard

set.seed(123)

Train_Index <- sample(seq_len(nrow(UniversalBank)),size = 3000)

Training <- UniversalBank[Train_Index, ]
Test <- UniversalBank[-Train_Index, ]
```

#Question A

Creation of a pivot table with "CC" variable as the rows and "Online" and "Personal Loan" variables as columns.
```{r}
Pivot_A <-xtabs(~ CC+`Personal Loan`+Online, data=Training)
```

Organizing the rows and columns of the pivot table then printing the results.
```{r}
Pivot_A <-ftable(Pivot_A, row.vars=c("CC", "Personal Loan"), col.vars = "Online")

print(Pivot_A)
```



#Question B

Extracting the counts from the pivot table and then calculating the probability.
```{r}
Pivot_A_Counts <-xtabs(~ CC+`Personal Loan`+Online, data=Training)

Probability_B <-Pivot_A_Counts["1","1","1"]/sum(Pivot_A_Counts["1", ,"1"])

print(Probability_B)

```
The probability the customer will accept the loan offer is roughly 10.7%


#Question C

Creating two separate pivot tables, the first having "Personal Loan" as rows and "Online" as columns and the other having "Personal Loan" as rows and "CC" as columns.
```{r}
Pivot_Online <-table(`Personal Loan`=Training$`Personal Loan`, Online=Training$Online)
print(Pivot_Online)

pivot_cc <-table(`Personal Loan`=Training$`Personal Loan`, CC=Training$CC)
print(pivot_cc)

```

#Question D

Creating variables calculating the six probabilities.
```{r}
P1 <-mean(Training$CC[Training$`Personal Loan`==1]==1)
P2 <-mean(Training$Online[Training$`Personal Loan`==1]==1)
P3 <-mean(Training$`Personal Loan`==1)
P4 <-mean(Training$CC[Training$`Personal Loan`==0]==1)
P5 <-mean(Training$Online[Training$`Personal Loan`==0]==1)
P6 <-mean(Training$`Personal Loan`== 0)
```

Collecting the results in a single variable and displaying them.
```{r}
Results <- c("i."=P1, "ii." = P2, "iii."=P3, "iv."=P4, "v."=P5, "vi." = P6)

print(round(Results, 6))
```

#Question E

Combining the results from Question D to be put into the Naive Bayes formula.
```{r}
NB1 <-P1*P2*P3
NB2 <-P4*P5*P6
Probability_E <-NB1/(NB1+NB2)
print(Probability_E)
```

#Question F

The Naive Bayes model is more accurate because it has a better percentage compared to the original data set.


#Question G

All entries are needed for computing P(Loan = 1 | CC = 1, Online = 1).

Converting variables for classification then training the Naive Bayes model using "CC" and "Online".
```{r}
Training$`Personal Loan` <-factor(Training$`Personal Loan`, levels=c(0,1))

Test$`Personal Loan` <-factor(Test$`Personal Loan`, levels=c(0,1))

NB_Model <- naiveBayes(`Personal Loan`~CC+Online,data=Training)

#print(NB_Model)

#print(NB_Model$tables)

#print(NB_Model$apriori)
```

Predicting the probabilities on the "Test" data using customers with CC = 1 and Online = 1
```{r}
NB_Predictions <-predict(NB_Model, newdata=Test, type="raw")

Selected <-Test$CC==1&Test$Online==1

print(head(NB_Predictions[Selected, , drop = FALSE]))
```
[1,1] = 0.1156935
Probability from Question E: [1] 0.1105637

We achieved a slightly higher percentage from the Naive Bayes model trained on the training data.
